subject: Game Theory
title: Tacit Collusion
description: A micro-lesson that makes Tacit Collusion usable.

hook.text: What if firms coordinate without ever speaking? Tacit collusion uses signals instead of agreements.

buildup.text: A market leader raises prices. Other firms follow within days. No meeting, no contract, no evidence.

discovery.text: Price leadership works because followers know that matching avoids a destructive price war.

twist.text: Tacit collusion is legal. Antitrust law requires an explicit agreement—parallel behavior alone isn't enough.

climax.text: Airlines, cement, and banking often show parallel pricing. Regulators suspect collusion but can't prove it.

punchline.text: No meeting needed. Just follow the leader.

quiz.question: Why is tacit collusion hard to prosecute?
options: There's no explicit agreement to prove
